prompt: For a Bloom filter with fixed memory and insertion count, why can adding too many hash functions increase false positives?

options.text: Every extra hash function deletes previously inserted keys.
False positives are impossible in an insert-only filter.
options.explanation: The guarantee concerns false negatives under stated conditions, not false positives.

options.text: A positive answer proves a key was inserted.
options.explanation: Other keys can set all of the queried positions.

options.text: More inserted bits make the filter increasingly full.
options.explanation: Extra checks help initially, but crowding eventually outweighs that benefit.

workedExample: Two effects compete: more positions must match for a query, but insertion also sets more positions. Choose a suitable trade-off for bits per key, and confirm positive results with the exact backing data when correctness matters.
